questions.corrige_markdown:
The terms $1, 4, 7, \ldots, 121$ (for $r = 0, 1, \ldots, 40$) form an arithmetic progression with first term $a = 1$ (at $r = 0$), common difference $d = 3$, and $n = 41$ terms. The last term is $l = 3(40) + 1 = 121$.

Use $S_n = \dfrac n2(a + l)$:
$$S_{41} = \frac{41}{2}(1 + 121) = 41 \times 61 = 2501.$$
Check with standard sums: $\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{40}(3r + 1) = 3\cdot\frac{40 \cdot 41}{2} + 41 = 2460 + 41 = 2501$.
$$\boxed{2501}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: A class of 9 students and a teacher is out on a field trip. On arrival at a car park they found out that there is only one taxi available to take them to their destination. Given that the taxi can carry only four passengers, find the number of ways that the 6 who will trek can be selected if the teacher must go by taxi. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
There are $9 + 1 = 10$ people. The taxi takes 4 of them, so the other $10 - 4 = 6$ trek; choosing the trekkers settles who rides.

If the teacher must go by taxi, the teacher is not among the 6 trekkers, so the 6 trekkers are chosen from the 9 students (equivalently, the teacher takes 3 of the 9 students in the taxi):
$$\binom96 = \binom93 = \frac{9 \times 8 \times 7}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 84.$$
$$\boxed{84 \text{ ways}}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: A class of 9 students and a teacher is out on a field trip. On arrival at a car park they found out that there is only one taxi available to take them to their destination. Given that the taxi can carry only four passengers, find the number of ways that the 6 who will trek can be selected if the teacher will not go by taxi. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
If the teacher does not go by taxi, the teacher is one of the 6 trekkers. The other 5 trekkers are chosen from the 9 students (equivalently, the taxi takes 4 of the 9 students):
$$\binom95 = \binom94 = \frac{9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 126.$$
$$\boxed{126 \text{ ways}}$$
Check: the two cases are exhaustive and disjoint, and $84 + 126 = 210 = \dbinom{10}{4}$, the total number of ways of choosing the 4 taxi passengers from the 10 people.
